paragraphs: Chapter 846
Episode 210. Memories of the Past - Murakan (5)
Losing and regaining consciousness several times a day.
Those days kept going. Occasionally, comrades, including Diana, visited the sickbed, but Murakan had little communication with them.
January 1, 800.
Runcandel and Zipple officially announced a truce to the world.
People guessed that Zipple, who had been overwhelmingly advantageous, abruptly ended the war because of Temar's return.
They said it was possible to end the war because he sacrificed his life to execute Elona Zipple.

However, in the memory of the saints, the names of Temar and Elona were quickly forgotten. The Tower of Tales easily changed the perception of ordinary people who had no power of existence and no resistance to manipulation.
Only the members of Runcandel and Zipple remembered the two.

"It's just a fake truce. Murakan, Zipple is still bloodshot trying to find the lord's body. They tried to humiliate us by offering surrender conditions, and they're unusually obsessed with the lord's body."
When Lokia said that, Murakan barely opened his eyes and looked at her.
"Lokia..."
"They keep raiding areas presumed to be the lord's tomb. Actually, we don't know where the lord is buried. So we're always moving later than they are."
Murakan did not answer for a while and thought about Temar's death. In the end, he had accepted the fact that he had died.
But the reality that Murakan had to accept was not the end.
"Diana... What about Diana."

"She died. While trying to guard the lord's tomb yesterday. Well, not exactly trying to guard the tomb. As I just said, we don't even know where that tomb is. We just confirmed Zipple's troop movement, followed it, and a battle broke out. She, who was not in good health, pushed herself too hard."
Lokia said in a calm voice. Looking at her now, she was severely injured all over her body.
"Who else... survived besides... you."
"It's hard to confirm who is alive or dead. The most likely one would be Luciro."
Lokia raised magic in her palm and wiped away the murky energy that flowed from Murakan's mouth.
"...I don't have much time left to use magic like this. Zipple and their gods have cursed Runcandel. We can no longer use magic."
"Lieutenant Lokia, I'm worried that it would be a severe shock to Mr. Murakan. Let's inform him later."
"Is that so? Kin. A shock... that wouldn't be bad. It's about time for Murakan to pay the price."
"Lieutenant Lokia!"

"During the last fight of the Grand Duke, if this guy had fought alongside us, we wouldn't be in this mess. A false peace, a curse named impotence, fools scattered everywhere trying to protect the Duke's corpse. It's unbearable."
"Sir Murakan is not at fault. We lost because of the manipulation of history, not because someone is responsible."
"Even though you who are still blind don't know, I don't think so."
"With the whereabouts of the Steward and the Ten Knights uncertain, it is up to you, Lady Lokia, to lead the family."
"Yes, it's my responsibility now. But as soon as Lucina or any other survivor returns, I will retire from the family."
"What are you saying? You're going to abandon the family...?"
"I no longer have any aspirations in this family. Look Kin, we have lost a lot while fighting for Runcandel. And yet, you're asking us to fight more? What gives you the right?"
Kin could not answer.
"Be thankful that I am not leaving right away. The only reason I'm delaying retirement is because I can't bear to see the family disappear without a trace."
Lokia left her seat. Murakan fell back into sleep, buried in a new shell of sadness.
But no matter how often he escaped into sleep,
The moment when he had no choice but to kill his comrades was still vivid. Despite Temar's miracle, the miserable reality of Runcandel had not disappeared.
Eventually, Murakan began to act strangely.
One day, he started to wander around the stormy region as if he had sleepwalking disorder, sometimes walking through the halls in human form, and sometimes flying in his original form.
No one could stop him. The one time someone tried, he reacted violently.
Half a year passed like this. Lokia left the family, and the invisible war between Runcandel and Zipple continued.
Murakan's strange behavior also continued.
He was constantly going farther and then returning. Sometimes he would leave the sickbed for a few hours, sometimes for several days.
"I'm not sure if Lord Murakan is really okay. I'm afraid he might be targeted by Zipple's assassins."
"Lord Kin, we feel the same. Zipple has no reason to leave Lord Murakan alone. If he ever falls into their trap... I heard that he is practically unable to fight now, only able to fly."
"Even Hidden Palace probably can't help now. Are we just supposed to wait like this?"
As Kin and the Sicksols' concerns grew, Murakan's return took over a month for the first time.
"Did he not come back today either? What's the situation on the Zipple side?"
"There was still no news of Lord Murakan being seen in the Lutero Federation."
"Has no one seen him on our side or the empire?"
"Yes... There have been no reports from anywhere."
There were no reports of anyone seeing Murakan anywhere in the world.
The Black Sea.
At that time, Murakan was walking on the Black Sea. Since he started to move away from the sickbed, his subconsciousness was always pointing towards the Black Sea.
And finally, Murakan was able to meet someone somewhere in the Black Sea.
[Murakan… you managed to reach this place alive.]
The witch Helrum.
She looked down at Murakan from a tower that rose in the Black Sea.
[With your current state, you certainly cannot handle the monsters and remnants here.]
Helrum looked at Murakan and the depths of the Black Sea behind him, as if surprised by the fact.
She tried to estimate the possibility of Murakan being able to meet her in the Black Sea with his destroyed heart.
It was almost impossible.
[Whether someone blessed you, or your will was so transcendent... it deserves its due. So, what made you so desperate to find me?]
"Memories...."
[Memories?]
"Erase my memories...."
So that I can give up at last.
Upon Murakan's trailing words, the witch, surprised, widened her eyes, then gave a smile.
[You're asking me to erase the memories you're already forgetting. Isn't it a waste to ask me?]
Murakan nodded without hesitation.
[Alright, I'll grant it.]
When Murakan opened his eyes after hearing Helrum's voice, he was back on the bed in the fortress.
Murakan quickly remembered what he needed to do when he saw Kin and Sicksol entering the infirmary.
He reminded himself that he needed to recover his heart as much as possible until the thousand-year contractor appeared.
Hoooo....
Like ashes scattering, the scene from a thousand years ago was ending.
Jin was silent for a moment, watching Murakan and the ten knights. Murakan, out of his mind, wept, reaching out into the void.
What he was trying to grasp was the ten knights he had killed in those days. The images of Dranaks, Violo, and Frei from a thousand years ago filled Murakan's sight.
However, he could not hold the illusion caused by chaos. His arms flailed in the air.
"I made a mistake, forgive me...."

At Murakan's hoarse voice, the ten knights, reborn as guardians, lowered their heads momentarily. Their time of dissolution was imminent. Their bodies were slowly disappearing, scattering into particles.
"Ah, shit. Why does this bastard make us cry, causing such a fuss. I'm disappearing now, should I go crying? Ugh, sob!"
"That's right, ah, I hate this. Hooo, sob!"
As Dranaks and Violo spoke, Frei hugged Murakan from behind. Dranaks and Violo also embraced Frei and Murakan, breaking into tears.
"Murakan."
"Frei...? Is that you, Frei?"
"Yes, it's me. Frei."
"Frei, forgive me."
"We should ask for forgiveness. You protected us and we resented you for not knowing that."
"Forgiveness, what forgiveness, you bastard!"
"Yeah, you bastard!"
"Dranaks... Violo."
Soon, Murakan, who turned around, was able to face Frei, who was smiling brightly, and the two people crying.
His headache was forgotten due to the bright smile. The sight of his friends crying and hugging him seemed like a dream, making him blink several times.

Murakan also embraced them. Their voices, trembles, heartbeat, and body temperature hit his entire body. The chains that tortured Murakan for a thousand years were breaking one by one. He was finally able to face them head on.
However, he could not be consumed by joy alone.
"Guys, don't go. Where are you going?"
The dissolution of the ten knights was accelerating. As the energy particles escaped, their bodies noticeably blurred.
"We're not disappearing, we're going into your memories."
Don't say that, just stay.
Murakan tried to respond in this way, but his throat was choked and he couldn't speak.
"Murakan, it's a bit embarrassing to say this, but we will be watching and fighting together in your memories from now on."

"The real Jin is from our time, not you and the present Runcandel. Hey, Jin! Please take care of this guy. I don't know much about being a thousand-year contractor or whatever, but I like you. I can trust you."
Murakan felt the presence of his friends that touched him fading.
And Frei, somehow denying Murakan's refusal to part, stroked his head and gently kissed his lips.

"I'm proud to have loved you. Murakan, you protected us with difficulty, and you found us with difficulty. So, live courageously without falling into sorrow again. Please nod just once. That way, I think we can comfortably become your memories."
Murakan nodded.
Because if he didn't nod now, he would never be able to do so in the future.
He also smiled. Because if he didn't show his smile now, he wouldn't be able to show it in the future.
"Goodbye, Murakan."
With Frei's voice as the last, the scene in Ketam came to an end.
